raw_response:
I'm a 48-year-old farmer here in Quzhou County, and I've been back on the land for about four years now. Before that I worked construction down in Shijiazhuang, so I'm still learning some of the finer points, but I run a tight ship — 200 mu is too big to mess around with. I hire seasonal workers for the busy times and I rent a combine for harvest. My neighbor Old Wang has been farming thirty years and I watch what he does closely; he's the one who talked me into trying stevia on a small plot two years ago. It doesn't pay like wheat-maize, but it's steady money and the company buys it on contract.

Since it's early March now, my winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. That takes up most of my land — about 140 mu — and come early June I'll harvest it and immediately plant summer maize on the same fields. That turnaround is brutal, usually less than a week, so I have my machinery lined up already. I keep 40 mu for spring cabbage and 20 mu for stevia. The cabbage goes to the wholesale market in Handan, but it's labor-heavy, so I have to balance that against the labor I need for wheat topdressing and maize planting.

For the wheat, I put down compound fertilizer as base last fall, and now I need to topdress urea at jointing — usually around early April. I'm figuring about 10 more kg of nitrogen per mu on top of what I already applied, for a total around 20 kg N/mu. I'll irrigate three times: green-up now in March, jointing in April, and grain filling in May. The well water isn't cheap — it's metered — but you can't skip it and expect decent yield. I'm aiming for around 460 kg/mu. I'll spray herbicide once and keep an eye out for fusarium; if it turns wet I might need fungicide.

The maize will go in mid-June right behind the combine. I'll use hybrid seed — it's expensive at about 45 yuan/mu but worth it. Because the window is so tight, I do minimal tillage, maybe a light rotary pass, then plant. I'll put compound fertilizer down with the planter and probably topdress once at the big trumpet stage if the plants look hungry. Total nitrogen around 18 kg/mu. Two irrigations should do it unless it's a drought year. Yield target is 500 kg/mu.

The cabbage is on 40 mu, transplanted in mid-March. It's a heavy feeder so I give it more fertilizer — about 22 kg N/mu total, split three times. I irrigate five times and stay on top of pests because the cabbage worms will destroy you if you blink. I expect about 4,000 kg/mu. It's good money when the price holds, but I learned the hard way that you can't plant too much or you'll be scrambling for labor during wheat harvest.

Stevia is only 20 mu — the buyer gives me seedlings. It's lower input: about 10 kg N/mu, two fertilizer applications, three irrigations, and mainly just weed control. I expect about 180 kg/mu of dried leaves. The contract price is stable, which I like because it balances out the gamble I take with cabbage prices.

My big worry is labor scheduling. With only four of us at home and my wife also helping manage things, I hire out for cabbage transplanting, wheat harvest, and maize planting. I need cash reserves for that hired labor and for the diesel. Total input costs this season will run me about 148,000 yuan. I could push for higher yields with more fertilizer, but after four years I've learned that a guaranteed decent profit beats a big gamble.
